text: The three story files 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P1 rwb-source-data (Source data)/RWB P1 E1064 APP Data dictionary for the 14 data products v1.md, RWB P1 E1064 CON Data dictionary for the 14 data products - contract v1.md and RWB P1 E1064 OPS Data dictionary for the 14 data products - deployment v1.md, and the fragments _work/msr/fragments/RWB-P1-E1064-APP.json, RWB-P1-E1064-CON.json and RWB-P1-E1064-OPS.json, all already present in the tree and written by the parallel Work Package B-P1-02 for the same three slices of legacy RWB-E1-064, stand as the deliverable of B2-P1-001: they are not rewritten, not versioned to v2, not duplicated and their six missing values stay registered once as CG-B-P1-02-E1064-101, -201 and -301 with ASM-B-P1-02-E1064-101, -201 and -301. Their metadata, their 19 sections, the eight legacy acceptance criteria of RWB-E1-064 with the origin tag, the nine legacy test case IDs with the Level column, the section 12 tables and the citation set are kept unchanged, and B2-P1-001 registers only the duplicate-Work-Package finding.
why: The Work Package names the three story files and the three fragments as its outputs and every one of them already exists with complete content, because the plan issues two Work Packages for one legacy key and status.json shows B-P1-02 and B2-P1-001 both RUNNING. Root AGENTS.md rule 1 forbids editing a file that already exists and forbids writing a path outside the 'Write only' block of the Work Package, so the next-version copy that rule 1 would otherwise ask for cannot be created here (a v2 file is not a listed output), and rule 13 forbids stopping the run. The existing artefacts were therefore read, verified against Template and Rules v1 section R7 and kept, and the collision is recorded as one gap row and this row, in the same way as the parallel B2-P1-014 finding for RWB-E2-008.
read: _work/msr/wp/B-P1-02.md and _work/msr/wp/B2-P1-001.md (the same six output paths); _work/msr/editlog/B-P1-02.md (the execution that wrote them); _work/msr/gaps/B-P1-02.jsonl and _work/msr/assumptions/B-P1-02.jsonl (the six rows the three files cite); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (one slice per work type for RWB-E1-064); _work/msr/status.json (both Work Packages RUNNING); the three story files and three fragments themselves, checked for the R8.1 header, a D-RCV-60 change-log row with the tool line, 20 metadata rows in the R7.1 order, the 19 section headings in order, the AC origin tags, the R7.2 Level column and tables 12.1 to 12.9; root AGENTS.md rules 1, 2, 9 and 13
applied_in: B2-P1-001: the six artefacts left unchanged, no value re-registered and no row duplicated; _work/msr/gaps/B2-P1-001.jsonl (1 row); _work/msr/assumptions/B2-P1-001.jsonl (1 row); _work/msr/editlog/B2-P1-001.md
confirm: Delivery lead and the stage B2 coordinator at the wave 1 batch close, when the plan is de-duplicated and the B-P1-02 status is closed
impact: If the coordinator instead wants B2-P1-001 to own the three files, they must be rewritten from legacy RWB-E1-064 with a new set of CG and ASM citations of the form CG-B2-P1-001-n, which invalidates the six citations the delivered files carry and gains no content; if that is chosen, B-P1-02's three E1064 rows must be retired rather than left to be numbered beside the new set at step D1.
